exp_janus_role: Software Developer | Industrial Automation & Systems Integration
exp_janus_summary:
Development and evolution of software solutions for industrial automation, asset tracking and systems integration. I work primarily with C#, .NET and WPF, participating in applications that connect software services, databases, identification devices and monitoring systems in industrial environments.

My work covers application development and maintenance, integration between services and devices, data processing and troubleshooting in distributed systems. I work with technologies and protocols such as MQTT, UDP, GPS, RFID/AEI and LoRaWAN to facilitate communication between components and ensure the availability and consistency of information.

I also participate in the analysis of technical problems, failure investigation, log review, communication diagnostics and interaction with services, servers and SQL databases. This experience allowed me to deepen my understanding of existing architectures, communication between components and the overall operation of production software systems.
exp_gestioner_summary:
Backend development focused on building applications and services, with an emphasis on C#, ASP.NET and API design. I participated in the development of server-side features, the implementation of business logic and the exposure of services for communication between applications and their respective data layers.

I worked on the administration and management of databases, including SQL queries, data organization and tasks related to their maintenance. I also used different tools and architectural approaches to develop solutions, understand the separation of responsibilities between components and adapt the implementation to the needs of each system.

This experience consolidated my knowledge in backend development, API design and integration, data persistence and application organization, strengthening my ability to work across different architectures and approach problems from a comprehensive technical perspective.
case_finance_problem: Managing personal expenses, due dates, payments and shared expenses from a mobile application, while keeping data accessible even without an internet connection.
case_finance_role: Mobile Developer. Design and implementation of the application with React Native, Expo and TypeScript, including business logic, local authentication, data persistence, UI components and automated testing.
case_finance_decisions: Offline-first design with on-device persistence and independent data spaces per account. Separation between domain, data access, authentication, hooks and UI components. Monetary amounts are represented as integers in cents to avoid floating-point precision errors. Credentials are validated locally and passwords are stored as salted hashes. The experience includes light and dark themes, animations, sounds and haptic feedback.
case_finance_outcome: Mobile application in development for Android and iOS, with local sign-up and sign-in, expense management, statistics, settings, budgets and automated testing for business rules and main flows. The next planned step is the implementation of local due-date notifications.
case_samaritana_problem: Develop an online store that makes it easy to browse and select cleaning products, with a clear shopping experience and a technical foundation prepared to evolve.
case_samaritana_role: Full-Stack Developer. Frontend development with React and TypeScript, and backend development through a REST API with ASP.NET Core. Solution organization using Clean Architecture.
case_samaritana_decisions: Separation between frontend and backend through a REST API. Backend organization with Clean Architecture to delimit responsibilities and ease maintenance. Use of TanStack Query for query management, React Hook Form and Zod for forms and validation, and reusable UI components to maintain a consistent experience.
case_samaritana_outcome: Full-stack application deployed, with the frontend published on Vercel and the backend built on ASP.NET Core. The implementation and functional scope should be documented according to the features actually completed.
